review.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
review.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

review.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
review.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. NON-VACUITY, three independent weakenings, each reverted after measuring: (a) letting an absent observation read as an empty one AND relaxing the product-name match to the substring 'liberty' fails 2 of 30 -- the check-never-run case and the Liberty Insurance Helper case; (b) pointing CERTIFICATION_SECTION at a heading the document does not have fails 4 of 30 across three suites, which is the derivation proving it is a derivation; (c) the entry-point guard was found by this suite rather than reasoned about -- process.argv[1].endsWith('lifecycle.mjs') also matches test-lifecycle.mjs, so importing the module to test parseArguments ran the harness and exited the test process with code 2. It is now compared by resolved path. WHAT NO TEST HERE CLAIMS: nothing in this suite observes a Windows machine. It tests the decisions -- which cases exist, who owns them, what counts as residue, whether an upgrade preserved content -- and one case runs the real script on this Linux container and asserts it exits non-zero with 'refusing to run on'. UNVERIFIED: every msiexec path, because no msiexec ran.

build.evidence: npm run build (turbo) at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7: Tasks 12 successful, 12 total, exit 0. STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN DRESSED UP: that run was FULL TURBO, entirely cache-hit, because this task's surface is scripts/windows/**, e2e/windows/** and one line of package.json's scripts block -- none of which is a build input for any workspace. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous and saying otherwise would be the kind of green mark this project refuses. What actually exercises this round's code: node scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs --plan runs on this platform and prints all six section-F cases with their owners and procedures, exit 0; node scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs --msi nowhere.msi exits 2 with 'refusing to run on linux'; and the 30-case suite recorded under the unit gate. The MSI itself cannot be built here -- the Rust toolchain in this container targets x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu only -- so no installer was produced and none of F1 to F4 was executed.
